Locally Adaptive Prediction Intervals

Source: R/gam_adaptive_pi.R
gam_adaptive_pi.Rd

Prediction intervals whose width follows the local scatter around the monotone GAM, calibrated by cross-validated conformal prediction.

Computes prediction intervals for a monotonically constrained GAM whose width varies along the source RT with the local scatter of the calibration compounds.

Usage

gam_adaptive_pi(rt_matrix, newdata, alpha = 0.05, n_folds = 5)

Arguments

rt_matrix

A 2-column matrix [rt_source, rt_target].

newdata

Numeric vector of x-values for predictions.

alpha

Significance level (default 0.05 for 95% PI).

n_folds

Number of cross-validation folds (default 5).

Value

A matrix with 3 columns: [predicted, lower, upper].

Details

Algorithm:

  1. Fit the monotone GAM (fit_gam_mono()).

  2. Cross-validated residuals: the compounds are split into n_folds folds, interleaved along the source RT. Each fold is predicted by the monotone spline refitted on the other folds with the smoothing parameter and weights of the full fit. If a fold cannot be refitted, its leave-one-out residuals of the unconstrained GAM are used instead.

  3. Local scale s(x): a Gamma GAM (log link, REML, at most 5 basis functions) of the absolute cross-validated residuals, weighted by the sigmoid outlier weights so that single outliers do not widen the band locally. s(x) is floored at 30% of the global weighted scale.

  4. Calibration: the multiplier q is the split-conformal quantile (the ceiling((n + 1) * (1 - alpha))-th smallest value) of the normalized residuals |e| / s(x). With fewer than about 1 / alpha compounds this is their maximum.

  5. Interval: prediction +/- q * s(x). Each bound is made non-decreasing by isotonic regression, which keeps lower <= prediction <= upper. The lower bound is truncated at 0.

With few compounds the interval covers less than its nominal level: in a cross-validation benchmark on RepoRT pairs with 10-15 shared compounds a 95% interval covered about 86% (about 95% from 30 compounds up).

Because the residuals are out-of-fold, q already includes the uncertainty of the fitted curve, so no separate standard error term is added.

References

Lei, J., G'Sell, M., Rinaldo, A., Tibshirani, R. J. & Wasserman, L. (2018). Distribution-free predictive inference for regression. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 113(523), 1094-1111.
